subject: Re: Private deployment capability questionnaire — offline & VPC readiness
messages:
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Private deployment capability questionnaire — Acme RFP

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this RFP. As part of our procurement pack I need a concise, technical response to a set of ops/security questions focused on on-prem/VPC and air-gapped scenarios. Our requirements include:

- Fully offline installation options (no internet) with reproducible verification
- KMS/HSM support for key custody and rotation controls
- Network allow-listing and minimal external egress for licensing or telemetry
- Patch/upgrade process for air-gapped clusters
- Logging, audit trails, and tamper-evident evidence for auditors

Could you please reply with a short capability table and any step-by-step checklist we can attach to the RFP? Also indicate any constraints (hardware, supported OS, required runtime privileges).

We would like the response by EOD Monday PST.

Best,
Jamie
Jamie Ortiz
Lead Information Security Engineer
Acme Corporation

From: olga.petrov@redwood.example
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: mark.li@acme-corp.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment capability questionnaire — Acme RFP

Jamie —

Thanks, we can cover the items you listed. Below is a concise capability summary tailored to air-gapped and VPC/on-prem deployments, plus an attached offline installation checklist and a verification script we recommend for auditor use. I also attached an architecture diagram that maps network flows for the on-prem package.

Capability summary (high-level)
- Offline installer: Supported. We provide a reproducible installation bundle (tarball) that includes runtime, model artifacts (optional), and a signed manifest. Installation can be performed from removable media or local repository; no outbound internet is required.
- Installer verification: We sign all release bundles using our private signing key. We provide a public verification utility that checks the manifest signature and checksums for all packages. For air-gapped validation, the attached rwd_airgap_verification_script.sh automates checksum verification and service smoke tests.
- KMS/HSM integration: Supported via configuration. On-prem deployment can integrate with customer HSMs that support PKCS#11 or cloud KMS adapters (for VPC). We support envelope encryption; keys can be rotated without full re-encrypts using key-wrapping.
- Minimal egress design: Licensing checks can be operated in a completely offline mode with license files embedded in the bundle; optional telemetry/usage reporters can be disabled. When telemetry is enabled, it is configurable to use a customer-controlled collector endpoint.
- Patch and upgrade process: Offline upgrades are supported via staged bundles and delta patches. We provide a documented process for applying updates offline using the same signed bundle mechanism; upgrades include pre/post hooks for compatibility checks and automated rollback on failure.
- Logging and audit evidence: All control-plane actions, config changes, and admin logins write to append-only audit logs. Audit logs can be exported to local SIEMs; immutable retention and cryptographic signing of logs are supported.
- Supported platforms & requirements: RHEL 8/9, Ubuntu 20.04+, and Debian 11+. Minimum cluster footprint: 3 nodes (control plane/masters) + worker nodes depending on throughput. Hardware: x86_64, NVIDIA GPUs (for model serving) or CPU-only mode for constrained environments.

Constraints and notes
- Model artifacts: If you require prepackaged model weights in the offline bundle, we will need an export authorization and size planning (weights can be sizable).
- Initial license activation: Can be performed via an offline license file; we recommend site-specific license keys distributed with the bundle.
- HSM firmware/driver compatibility: Customer must ensure PKCS#11-compatible interface is available on host OS.

Attachments included:
- rwd_offline_installation_checklist_v1.0.pdf (step-by-step offline install checklist)
- rwd_onprem_architecture_diagram_acme.pdf (network/dataflow diagram)
- rwd_airgap_verification_script.sh (sample verification script)
- soc2-summary-redwood-2026.pdf (SOC 2 summary for auditor context)

I'll follow up with a short checklist excerpt inline to make quick review easier.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.example

(Quick inline checklist excerpt for procurement & auditors)

Offline installation checklist (excerpt)
1) Verify hardware and OS prerequisites per supported platforms.
2) Transfer signed bundle to air-gapped host (scoped removable media or secure network share).
3) Validate bundle signature: sha256 checksums + our signed manifest.
4) Run verifier: rwd_airgap_verification_script.sh (performs checksum, service-start smoke test, and sample inference call against a bundled minimal model).
5) Install HSM driver and configure PKCS#11 path in redwood.conf (if using HSM).
6) Apply license file to the management plane; verify license activation locally.
7) Start services in staging; run automated upgrade/rollback test (we provide a test delta bundle).
8) Export audit logs and sign using local key for retention.

Air-gap verification notes
- The verification script is self-contained and requires only a POSIX shell and openssl available on the host. It outputs signed verification artifacts you can archive for auditors.
- We recommend completing a dry-run: install on a mirrored air-gapped staging network to exercise HSM integration, network ACLs, and backup/restore.

If you would like, Dylan can run a short remote workshop with your infra team to walk through the checklist and verify the installer in a lab.

Regards,
Olga
